notes: Coffee with Sarah. MedLoop is preparing to raise a $4M seed round in November and she explicitly asked if I know healthcare investors - she wants intros to funds that do digital health. They've signed 2 hospital pilots. Also looking for an experienced enterprise sales advisor who has sold into health systems, since none of the founders has done that. She offered to connect any founder I know with clinicians from her advisory network.

Lunch with Michael. Northbeam just closed Fund III. He said he wants to see more early-stage digital health deals - seed and Series A, especially AI tools for hospitals. He's actively looking and asked me to send good founders his way. Also mentioned his portfolio companies always need help with go-to-market and brand.

Caught up with Priya. She left HealthGrid in the spring after 9 years running enterprise sales into hospital systems. She told me she wants 2-3 advisory roles with early-stage healthcare startups, ideally with equity. Very open to meeting founders.

Zoom with David. Ledgerline is hiring a VP of Engineering - their last search fell through and he needs someone by Q1 who has scaled payments infrastructure. He also mentioned he knows a lot of people in the payments regulatory world and is happy to help founders navigate compliance.

Elena reached out privately. She's quietly exploring VP Engineering roles at fintech startups - wants to lead a team building payments infrastructure. Please keep it confidential. She's led the Paystream ledger rebuild for 3 years.

Dinner with Tom. Routewise is focused on landing mid-size retail customers for their delivery routing software - he'd love intros to operations leaders at retail chains. He was clear he does not want investor intros right now. He offered to share their pricing playbook with any SaaS founder.

Met Grace at the retail ops summit. Brightmart is evaluating delivery and routing software vendors this quarter - their current system is failing and she has budget approved for Q4. She asked if I know any good vendors.
Chatted briefly with Marcus at a conference reception. He's a startup CEO. We didn't get into much detail - mostly talked about the conference talks.
Ran into James. He mentioned that a friend of his is looking for healthcare investors, but didn't say who. Coinvault itself is doing fine and he didn't ask for anything.
Hannah said Sequel is focused on Series A and B healthcare and fintech companies with at least $2M ARR. Reiterated she doesn't look at seed deals.
Olivia wants to launch a founder-led podcast for Bloom & Co to build B2B wholesale relationships. She's looking for a production agency that understands B2B and wants to launch by January.
Ben's agency Signal Studio produces B2B podcasts end-to-end - strategy, guest booking, editing. They have capacity for two new clients this fall and he asked me for referrals.
Kevin said Tallgrass needs office space in Austin before their January move. Asked if I knew any commercial real estate brokers.
Quick call with Aisha. Kinfolk is still deciding whether to build a provider partnerships program next year - nothing concrete yet and she didn't ask for anything. Said to check back in the new year.

Lunch with Ryan. Clearpath has a startup practice now and he's handled a dozen seed and Series A financings this year. He offered to review term sheets for free for any founder I know who's raising - he'd rather help early than clean up a bad deal later.

Coffee with Sofia. Vantage Growth just finished two go-to-market engagements and has room for one or two more clients this winter. She specifically wants seed-stage, VC-backed B2B startups and asked me to send any founders or investors who need GTM help her way.

Dinner with Daniel. Nimbus's support team is drowning since they doubled their customer count - he's shopping for a customer support platform before January and wants something that integrates with their own product data. Asked if I knew any good vendors.
Laura is starting parental leave next week and will be out until summer. Promised I'd check in when she's back. Helix is running two Phase 2 trials.

Chris called to catch up. Summit Talent now focuses on VP-level engineering searches at fintech companies and he's placed four this year. He offered to help any founder with a hard exec engineering search, and said he's happy to just give advice even if they don't hire him.

Coffee with Natalie. She's writing $25-50K checks into pre-seed and seed consumer and edtech companies and wants to back more founders building for kids and families. She doesn't invest in healthcare, crypto, or B2B software.

Omar called. Packwise has partnerships with about 40 third-party warehouses and he offered to introduce any e-commerce founder I know who's outgrowing their fulfillment setup. He didn't need anything.

Coffee with Megan. Cobalt Cloud is planning a full rebrand ahead of their Series B announcement in February - new name for the product line, site, and visual identity. Their last agency didn't understand infrastructure buyers, so she's looking for a brand design studio that has done B2B tech work.

Ran into Jorge at a fintech meetup. Lumen just finished money transmitter licensing in 12 states and he's happy to walk any early-stage fintech founder through how they did it. He didn't ask for anything.

Coffee with Emily. Ardent Design just wrapped a rebrand for a developer tools company and has an opening starting in December. She wants more B2B tech clients, ideally a full rebrand rather than a one-off logo, and asked me for referrals.
Holiday party catch-up with Patrick. Mostly talked about his kids' hockey season and his move to the Seattle office. Nothing work-related came up.
Rachel runs a recruiting firm and asked me to introduce her to as many startup CEOs as possible so she can pitch her recruiting services.
Quick call with Victor. Arcadia only does growth buyouts of profitable healthcare services companies, $20M+ EBITDA. He was clear they don't look at venture-stage startups or software.

Zoom with Isabel. Quill CX has lost two enterprise deals this quarter because they couldn't get through security reviews - they need to get SOC 2 done and nobody on the team has been through it. She'd love to talk to a security leader who's done it before. They're also looking for more mid-market customers.
Lunch with Samuel. He's started advising early-stage founders on their first SOC 2 and enterprise security reviews - he offered a free hour to any founder I know who's stuck on it.

Coffee with Zoe. Sprout Kids is raising a $1.2M pre-seed in December for their early-reading app - 8,000 families on the waitlist. She wants angels who know consumer subscriptions and edtech, not big funds yet. She's also looking for an advisor who's built a consumer brand.
